claims.claim: Uts2r3 was previously implicated in spine morphology.
claims.source: One of those, Uts2r3, was previously implicated in spine morphology (Zhang et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claims.claim: The uts2r3b1436 mutant line harbors a 178-amino acid deletion after the third amino acid.
claims.source: To systematically compare the effects of Uts2r3 receptor mutation with loss of Urp1 and Urp2, we generated a uts2r3 mutant line harboring a 178-amino acid deletion after the third amino acid, significantly disrupting the protein (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: This is supported by the mutation description in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: uts2r3b1436 mutants undergo normal axial straightening as embryos.
claims.source: Like urp1∆P;urp2∆P double mutants, these uts2r3b1436 mutants underwent normal axial straightening as embryos (Figure 1Ei) and went on to exhibit spinal curves as adults (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, Figure 2—video 8).
claims.evidence: This is supported by imaging data in Figure 1Ei.

claims.claim: uts2r3b1436 mutants exhibit spinal curves as adults.
claims.source: Like urp1∆P;urp2∆P double mutants, these uts2r3b1436 mutants underwent normal axial straightening as embryos (Figure 1Ei) and went on to exhibit spinal curves as adults (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, Figure 2—video 8).
claims.evidence: This is supported by µCT data in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: uts2r3b1436 mutants and urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants have similar Cobb angles, though curves in urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants are slightly more severe.
claims.source: Cobb angle measurements showed that uts2r3b1436 mutants and urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants were similar, though curves in urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants were slightly more severe (Figure 2D–E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Cobb angle measurements in Figure 2D–E.

claims.claim: uts2r3b1436 mutants show mostly caudally located curves, especially in the most rostral of the caudal vertebrae.
claims.source: Like urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants, uts2r3b1436 mutants showed mostly caudally located curves, especially in the most rostral of the caudal vertebrae (Figure 2F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by curve position data in Figure 2F.

claims.claim: Urp1 and Urp2 control spine morphology largely by signaling through Uts2r3.
claims.source: Thus, although we cannot rule out minor roles for other UT receptors, these data suggest that Urp1 and Urp2 control spine morphology largely by signaling through Uts2r3.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the similarity of phenotypes between urp1/urp2 double mutants and uts2r3 mutants.

claims.claim: Several types of human spinal curves onset during adolescent growth.
claims.source: Several types of human spinal curves onset during adolescent growth (Cheng et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is established medical knowledge supported by citation.

claims.claim: Subtle curves first become apparent in urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants between 9 and 11 days post fertilization.
claims.source: Subtle curves first became apparent between 9 and 11 days pf (dpf), corresponding to a standard length between 3.9±0.7 mm and 5.9±0.4 mm (mean ± s.d.; Figure 3A–B, Figure 3—video 1), a stage when adolescents were rapidly growing (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by imaging and growth curve data in Figure 3A–C.

claims.claim: Curves are evident in all urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants by 13 dpf.
claims.source: By 13 dpf (standard length 6.2±0.3 mm), curves were evident in all urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants and progressively worsened up to 17 dpf (8.3±0.4 mm) when we ended this analysis (Figure 3A–B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by imaging data in Figure 3A–B.

claims.claim: At 1 mpf, five of seven urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants exhibit a significant curve in the pre-caudal vertebrae in addition to a caudal curve.
claims.source: At 1 mpf, we assessed urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants by µCT and found variability in curve position and amplitude (Figure 3D). Notably, at this stage, five of seven mutants exhibited a significant curve in the pre-caudal vertebrae, in addition to a caudal curve (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1Ai-Bii).
claims.evidence: This is supported by µCT data in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Pre-caudal curves are rare in urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants at 3 mpf.
claims.source: Since pre-caudal curves were rare in mutants at 3 mpf (Figure 2B and F), this suggested that curve location is dynamic and that pre-caudal curves form then resolve or shift in some mutants as they grow to adulthood.
claims.evidence: This is supported by curve position data in Figure 2F.

claims.claim: Curve location is dynamic in urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants as they grow to adulthood.
claims.source: Since pre-caudal curves were rare in mutants at 3 mpf (Figure 2B and F), this suggested that curve location is dynamic and that pre-caudal curves form then resolve or shift in some mutants as they grow to adulthood.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that pre-caudal curves are common at 1 mpf but rare at 3 mpf.

claims.claim: Calcein staining revealed no defects in vertebral patterning or spacing in urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants at 10 dpf.
claims.source: Staining of juveniles with the vital dye calcein revealed no defects in vertebral patterning or spacing in urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants at 10 dpf (4.5–6 mm standard length [Figure 3C]) (Figure 3G).
claims.evidence: This is supported by calcein staining data in Figure 3G.

claims.claim: urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants exhibit more variable vertebral length aspect ratios than wild type.
claims.source: Vertebral body length and height aspect ratios were 1.00±0.007 (mean ± s.d.) and 0.99±0.007, respectively, for wild type (n=4; Figure 3F). By contrast, urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants exhibited more variable vertebral length aspect ratios (0.97±0.03, p=0.022; Bartlett's test for equal variances, Figure 3F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by vertebral morphometry data in Figure 3F.

claims.claim: Vertebral height aspect ratios in urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants are not significantly different from controls.
claims.source: Vertebral height aspect ratios in mutants (1.00±0.006) were not significantly different to controls (p=0.745, Figure 3F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by vertebral morphometry data in Figure 3F.

claims.claim: Small changes in vertebral shape in urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants are likely due to the presence of curves rather than causative of curves.
claims.source: These data are consistent with subtle vertebral shape defects at the points of curvature in urp1∆Purp2∆P mutants. However, we do not observe vertebral fusions or missing or transformed appendages, suggesting that vertebral defects do not underlie spinal curves; instead, small changes in vertebral shape are likely due to the presence of curves themselves rather than causative of curves in the first place.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that vertebral defects are subtle and similar to what occurs in non-congenital human scoliosis.

claims.claim: There are no significant differences in curve penetrance or severity between males and females in urp1∆P;urp2∆P and uts2r3b1436 mutants.
claims.source: Additionally, we parsed our phenotypic data for sex since spinal curves often show sex bias in severity in humans (Cheng et al., 2015), something which has been recapitulated in some zebrafish spinal curve mutants (Marie-Hardy et al., 2021). However, in both urp1∆P;urp2∆P and uts2r3b1436 mutants, we found no significant differences in curve penetrance or severity between males and females (Figure 2E').
claims.evidence: This is supported by sex-parsed data in Figure 2E'.

claims.claim: cfap298tm304 mutants exhibit reduced cilia motility in the central canal.
claims.source: The cfap298tm304 line harbors a temperature-sensitive mutation in cfap298, a gene required for cilia motility in several organisms including humans (Austin-Tse et al., 2013; Bearce et al., 2022; Jaffe et al., 2016). cfap298tm304 mutants exhibit reduced cilia motility in the central canal and, if the resulting CTD is embryonically rescued by temperature shifts, develop adolescent-onset spinal curves (Grimes et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claims.claim: If the CTD of cfap298tm304 mutants is embryonically rescued by temperature shifts, they develop adolescent-onset spinal curves.
claims.source: cfap298tm304 mutants exhibit reduced cilia motility in the central canal and, if the resulting CTD is embryonically rescued by temperature shifts, develop adolescent-onset spinal curves (Grimes et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work and by data in Figure 4.

claims.claim: cfap298tm304 mutants were argued to model an adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS)-like condition.
claims.source: These curves were argued to model an adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS)-like condition (Figure 4A–B, Figure 4—video 1; Grimes et al., 2016; Marie-Hardy et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claims.claim: urp1 and urp2 transcripts are significantly downregulated in cfap298tm304 mutants.
claims.source: Importantly, both urp1 and urp2 transcripts were significantly downregulated in cfap298tm304 mutants (Figure 1F) suggesting that spinal curves in cfap298tm304 might be the result of reduced Urp1/Urp2 expression.
claims.evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data in Figure 1F.

claims.claim: cfap298tm304 mutants are more severely curved than urp1∆P;urp2∆P or uts2r3b1436 mutants.
claims.source: First, we calculated dorso-ventral Cobb angles, which revealed that cfap298tm304 mutants were more severely curved (average total Cobb angle: 260.4±32.7°) than either urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants (197.5±38.9°) or uts2r3b1436 mutants (146.1±47.4°) (Figure 4E, Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1D–E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Cobb angle measurements in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: cfap298tm304 mutants show prominent dorsal-ventral curves in both pre-caudal and caudal vertebrae.
claims.source: Second, cfap298tm304 mutants showed prominent dorsal-ventral curves in the pre-caudal as well as caudal vertebrae, a distinct pattern compared with the predominantly caudal curves in urp1∆P;urp2∆P and uts2r3b1436 mutants (Figure 4A–C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by µCT data and curve position analysis in Figure 4 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: cfap298tm304 mutants exhibit significant lateral curvature of the spine, often with spinal twisting.
claims.source: Third, cfap298tm304 mutants exhibited significant lateral curvature of the spine, often with spinal twisting, a hallmark of AIS-like curves (Figure 4Fi–Fii, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is supported by dorsal view µCT data and lateral curvature quantitation in Figure 4Fi–Fii.

claims.claim: urp1∆P;urp2∆P and uts2r3b1436 mutants show planar curves with very minor or no lateral deviations.
claims.source: By contrast, urp1∆P;urp2∆P and uts2r3b1436 mutants showed planar curves, with very minor or no lateral deviations (Figure 4Fi–Fii, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is supported by dorsal view µCT data and lateral curvature quantitation in Figure 4Fi–Fii.

claims.claim: Cilia motility mutants and urotensin-deficient mutants exhibit distinct spinal curve phenotypes.
claims.source: These results demonstrated that cilia motility mutants and urotensin-deficient mutants exhibit distinct spinal curve phenotypes.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the quantitative differences in curve severity, position, and direction between mutant types.

claims.claim: The causes of spinal curves in cfap298tm304 mutants can only be partially explained by reduced Urp1/Urp2 expression.
claims.source: As such, the causes of spinal curves in cfap298tm304 mutants can only be partially explained by reduced Urp1/Urp2 expression.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that cfap298 mutants have more severe and different curves than urotensin-deficient mutants.

claims.claim: cfap298tm304;urp1∆P;urp2∆P triple mutants exhibit significant curves similar to cfap298tm304 single mutants.
claims.source: To further explore the relationship between cilia motility and urotensin peptides, we generated adult cfap298tm304;urp1∆P;urp2∆P triple mutants that were embryonically rescued by temperature shifts. Triple mutants exhibited significant curves, similar to cfap298tm304 single mutants (Figure 4D–E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–E, Figure 4—video 2; average total Cobb angle: 284.4±33.5°).
claims.evidence: This is supported by µCT data and Cobb angle measurements in Figure 4D–E.

claims.claim: The curves of cfap298tm304;urp1∆P;urp2∆P triple mutants are three-dimensional in nature, with both dorso-ventral and medio-lateral deviations, as well as incidences of spinal torsion.
claims.source: The curves of triple mutants were three-dimensional in nature, with both dorso-ventral and medio-lateral deviations, as well as incidences of spinal torsion (Figure 4Fi–Fii, Figure 4—figure supplement 1); curves were present in both pre-caudal and caudal vertebrae, as opposed to being more restricted to caudal vertebrae in urp1∆P;urp2∆P double mutants (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by µCT data in Figure 4Fi–Fii and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Motile cilia contribute to urotensin-dependent and urotensin-independent pathways controlling spine morphology.
claims.source: Overall, this suggests that motile cilia contribute to urotensin-dependent and urotensin-independent pathways controlling spine morphology.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that triple mutants have similar phenotypes to cfap298 single mutants.

claims.claim: Pkd2l1 is a polycystin family ion channel expressed in CSF-cNs.
claims.source: Pkd2l1 is a polycystin family ion channel expressed in CSF-cNs, the same cell type which expresses Urp1 and Urp2 (Figure 1D; Quan et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation and by in situ data in Figure 1D.

claims.claim: Pkd2l1 is responsible for flow-induced Ca2+ signaling in CSF-cNs.
claims.source: Pkd2l1 is responsible for flow-induced Ca2+ signaling in CSF-cNs (Böhm et al., 2016; Sternberg et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claims.claim: pkd2l1icm02 mutants exhibit normal early axis development.
claims.source: While pkd2l1icm02 mutants exhibited normal early axis development, they went on to develop mild kyphosis-like curves upon aging (Sternberg et al., 2018), a result we recapitulated after raising pkd2l1icm02 mutants on the same genetic background and under the same conditions as urotensin-deficient mutants for direct comparison (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claims.claim: pkd2l1icm02 mutants develop mild kyphosis-like curves upon aging.
claims.source: While pkd2l1icm02 mutants exhibited normal early axis development, they went on to develop mild kyphosis-like curves upon aging (Sternberg et al., 2018), a result we recapitulated after raising pkd2l1icm02 mutants on the same genetic background and under the same conditions as urotensin-deficient mutants for direct comparison (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation and by µCT data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–B.

claims.claim: pkd2l1icm02 mutants show very subtle curves in the pre-caudal vertebrae and absence of lateral deviation at 12 mpf.
claims.source: Notably, pkd2l1icm02 mutants showed very subtle curves in the pre-caudal vertebrae and absence of lateral deviation at 12 mpf but no obvious curves of any kind at 3 mpf (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A-B, Figure 4—videos 3–4).
claims.evidence: This is supported by µCT data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–B.

claims.claim: The mild kyphosis-like phenotype of pkd2l1icm02 mutants is highly distinct from urp1∆P;urp2∆P and uts2r3b1436 mutants.
claims.source: This mild kyphosis-like phenotype was therefore also highly distinct from urp1∆P;urp2∆P and uts2r3b1436 mutants.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of phenotypes across mutant lines.

claims.claim: urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants develop adolescent-onset curves without significant vertebral structural defects or sex bias.
claims.source: Overall, our phenotypic data show that urp1∆P;urp2∆P mutants develop adolescent-onset curves without significant vertebral structural defects or sex bias.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of findings from multiple experiments.

claims.claim: Urotensin pathway mutants most closely reflect a lordosis-like condition.
claims.source: Coupled to the consistently caudal location of curves at 3 mpf as well as the lack of lateral deviation, we suggest that urotensin pathway mutants most closely reflect a lordosis-like condition.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the phenotypic characteristics of the mutants.

claims.claim: Urotensin mutants are phenotypically distinct from established AIS-like (cfap298tm304) and kyphosis-like (pkd2l1icm02) models.
claims.source: In agreement, urotensin mutants were phenotypically distinct from established AIS-like (cfap298tm304) and kyphosis-like (pkd2l1icm02) models.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of comparative phenotypic analysis.

claims.claim: In sibling controls, Sspo localizes into a Reissner fiber throughout the central canal at 28 hpf.
claims.source: First, we assessed Sspo localization in the central canal of cfap298tm304 mutants at 28 hr pf (hpf). In sibling controls, Sspo localized into an RF throughout the central canal (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Sspo-GFP imaging data in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: cfap298tm304 mutants raised at restrictive temperatures lack Reissner fiber at 28 hpf.
claims.source: By contrast, cfap298tm304 mutants raised at restrictive temperatures, which exhibited reduced central canal cilia motility and CTD (Figure 1E; Bearce et al., 2022), lacked RF. Instead, Sspo was diffusely localized in the central canal in these mutants (Figure 5B), in agreement with previous work showing that cilia motility is required for RF assembly in embryos (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Sspo-GFP imaging data in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: Sspo is diffusely localized in the central canal in cfap298tm304 mutants at 28 hpf.
claims.source: By contrast, cfap298tm304 mutants raised at restrictive temperatures, which exhibited reduced central canal cilia motility and CTD (Figure 1E; Bearce et al., 2022), lacked RF. Instead, Sspo was diffusely localized in the central canal in these mutants (Figure 5B), in agreement with previous work showing that cilia motility is required for RF assembly in embryos (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Sspo-GFP imaging data in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: Sspo is diffuse in temperature upshifted cfap298tm304 mutants at 12 dpf.
claims.source: As in embryos, Sspo localized into a defined RF in the central canal in sibling controls (arrow head in Figure 5D) but was diffuse in temperature upshifted cfap298tm304 mutants, both in mutants that had yet to develop curves and those exhibiting subtle curves (Figure 5E, Figure 5H).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Sspo-GFP imaging data in Figure 5E.

claims.claim: Cilia motility is required for the initial formation of the Reissner fiber and for its maintenance.
claims.source: This demonstrates (1) that cilia motility is not only required for the initial formation of the RF but also for its maintenance; and (2) breakdown of the RF precedes curve onset in cilia motility-deficient mutants.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that RF breaks down in cfap298 mutants at 12 dpf before curves form.

claims.claim: Breakdown of the Reissner fiber precedes curve onset in cilia motility-deficient mutants.
claims.source: This demonstrates (1) that cilia motility is not only required for the initial formation of the RF but also for its maintenance; and (2) breakdown of the RF precedes curve onset in cilia motility-deficient mutants.
claims.evidence: This is supported by the observation that RF is disrupted at 12 dpf in cfap298 mutants before curves are fully formed.

claims.claim: Continued cilia motility maintains the Reissner fiber structure, and loss of the RF causes AIS-like curves in cilia motility mutants.
claims.source: This supports a model in which continued cilia motility maintains the RF structure, and loss of the RF causes AIS-like curves to develop in cilia motility mutants.
claims.evidence: This is a model inferred from the temporal relationship between RF breakdown and curve formation.

claims.claim: Sspo localizes normally into the Reissner fiber in the central canal at 28 hpf in uts2r3b1436 mutants.
claims.source: In agreement with that lack of axial straightening phenotype in uts2r3b1436 mutant embryos (Figure 1Ei), we found that Sspo localized normally into the RF in the central canal at 28 hpf in uts2r3b1436 mutants (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Sspo-GFP imaging data in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: Sspo forms an intact Reissner fiber in uts2r3b1436 mutants at 12 dpf as spinal curves are beginning to manifest.
claims.source: At 12 dpf, as spinal curves were beginning to manifest (Figure 5I), Sspo still formed an intact RF in uts2r3b1436 mutants (arrow head in Figure 5F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Sspo-GFP imaging data in Figure 5F.

claims.claim: Urotensin-associated curves are not caused by defective Reissner fiber formation.
claims.source: The fact that RF is present in uts2r3b1436 mutants as curves form suggests that urotensin-associated curves are not caused by defective RF formation.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that RF remains intact in uts2r3 mutants despite the presence of curves.

claims.claim: Large central canal cells with the appearance of CSF-cNs become GFP-positive in cfap298tm304 and uts2r3b1436 mutants at 12 dpf.
claims.source: While imaging Sspo-GFP at 12 dpf, we noted that in both cfap298tm304 mutants and uts2r3b1436 mutants, large central canal cells with the appearance of CSF-cNs became GFP-positive (arrows in Figure 5E–F), something we rarely observed in control fish (Figure 5D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Sspo-GFP imaging data in Figure 5E–F.

claims.claim: CSF-cNs may endocytose Sspo-GFP monomers in cfap298tm304 mutants where the RF has broken down and in uts2r3b1436 mutants where RF is making increasing contacts with CSF-cNs.
claims.source: We suggest that CSF-cNs may endocytose Sspo-GFP monomers in cfap298tm304 mutants where the RF has broken down and in uts2r3b1436 mutants where RF is likely to be making increasing numbers of contacts with CSF-cNs (Orts-Del'Immagine et al., 2020) owing to the onset of spinal curves.
claims.evidence: This is a hypothesis to explain the observation of GFP-positive CSF-cNs.

claims.claim: Urotensin II (UII) was first identified from the teleost urophysis.
claims.source: Urotensin II (UII) is a cyclic peptide that was first identified from the teleost urophysis (Pearson et al., 1980) and subsequently found to exist in amphibians (Conlon et al., 1992) and mammals (Coulouarn et al., 1998).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claims.claim: Urotensin II was subsequently found to exist in amphibians and mammals.
claims.source: Urotensin II (UII) is a cyclic peptide that was first identified from the teleost urophysis (Pearson et al., 1980) and subsequently found to exist in amphibians (Conlon et al., 1992) and mammals (Coulouarn et al., 1998).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: URP was isolated from the brains of rodents.
claims.source: A highly similar peptide, called URP was then isolated from the brains of rodents (Sugo et al., 2003).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claims.claim: UII and URP both signal via the UT, a G-protein-coupled receptor.
claims.source: UII and URP both signal via the UT, a G-protein-coupled receptor (Ames et al., 1999; Liu et al., 1999; Mori et al., 1999; Nothacker et al., 1999).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: UIIs, URPs, and UTs have been linked to cardiovascular function and inflammation.
claims.source: UIIs, URPs, and UTs have been linked to cardiovascular function and inflammation, but their roles in the development of morphology are little understood.
claims.evidence: This is general knowledge about urotensin function.

claims.claim: The roles of UIIs, URPs, and UTs in the development of morphology are little understood.
claims.source: UIIs, URPs, and UTs have been linked to cardiovascular function and inflammation, but their roles in the development of morphology are little understood.
claims.evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claims.claim: Urp1 and Urp2 function semi-redundantly to control spine morphology.
claims.source: In this study, we discovered a role for two of the URPs, Urp1 and Urp2, in zebrafish spine morphology. To do so, we generated urp1∆P and urp2∆P mutants that lacked the genetic region coding for the Urp1 and Urp2 peptides, respectively, then phenotyped skeletal morphology by µCT. This revealed that Urp1 and Urp2 function semi-redundantly to control spine morphology, with double mutants, as well as Uts2r3 receptor mutants, developing spinal curves in the caudal region during adolescent growth.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the main findings of the study.

claims.claim: The lack of major vertebral defects and the location and direction of curves suggest that urotensin-deficient mutants model a lordosis-like condition.
claims.source: The lack of major vertebral defects, the location and direction of the curves coupled with phenotypic differences compared with mutants that model AIS and kyphosis, suggested that urotensin-deficient mutants model a lordosis-like condition.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the phenotypic characteristics of the mutants.

claims.claim: RF breaks down prior to curve formation in the cilia motility cfap298tm304 mutant.
claims.source: We find that RF breaks down prior to curve formation in the cilia motility cfap298tm304 mutant.
claims.evidence: This is supported by Sspo-GFP imaging data in Figure 5.

claims.claim: RF breakdown is a major factor driving spinal curves in cfap298tm304 mutants.
claims.source: Given other studies linking presence of the RF with a linear body axis, this strongly suggests that RF breakdown is a major factor driving spinal curves in cfap298tm304 mutants.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the temporal relationship between RF breakdown and curve formation, along with previous studies.

claims.claim: Uts2r3-deficient mutants exhibit an intact Reissner fiber.
claims.source: By contrast, Uts2r3-deficient mutants exhibited an intact RF, demonstrating that curves are not formed by RF breakdown in urotensin pathway mutants and nor do the presence of curves significantly disrupt RF structure.
claims.evidence: This is supported by Sspo-GFP imaging data in Figure 5.

claims.claim: Curves are not formed by RF breakdown in urotensin pathway mutants.
claims.source: By contrast, Uts2r3-deficient mutants exhibited an intact RF, demonstrating that curves are not formed by RF breakdown in urotensin pathway mutants and nor do the presence of curves significantly disrupt RF structure.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that RF remains intact in uts2r3 mutants despite the presence of curves.

claims.claim: The presence of curves does not significantly disrupt RF structure in urotensin pathway mutants.
claims.source: By contrast, Uts2r3-deficient mutants exhibited an intact RF, demonstrating that curves are not formed by RF breakdown in urotensin pathway mutants and nor do the presence of curves significantly disrupt RF structure.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that RF remains intact in uts2r3 mutants despite the presence of curves.

claims.claim: Urotensin signals act downstream of RF function in controlling spine morphology.
claims.source: This coheres with a model in which urotensin signals act downstream of RF function in controlling spine morphology.
claims.evidence: This is a model inferred from the observation that RF is intact in urotensin mutants and that urp expression is controlled by RF.

claims.claim: urp1 and urp2 expression are controlled by RF function during embryonic phases.
claims.source: Similarly, urp1 and urp2 expression are known to be controlled by RF function during embryonic phases (Figure 1F; Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2020; Lu et al., 2020; Rose et al., 2020; Zhang et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations and by qRT-PCR data in Figure 1F.

claims.claim: Motile cilia mutants and sspo mutants exhibit three-dimensional spinal curves, with dorso-ventral and medio-lateral curvature.
claims.source: Intriguingly, motile cilia mutants and sspo mutants exhibit three-dimensional spinal curves, with dorso-ventral and medio-lateral curvature (Grimes et al., 2016; Lu et al., 2020; Rose et al., 2020; Troutwine et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

results.result: The authors generated urp1ΔP and urp2ΔP mutant zebrafish lines lacking the peptide coding sequences. Surprisingly, both single and double mutants, including maternal-zygotic double mutants, underwent normal embryonic axial straightening without exhibiting the curly tail down (CTD) phenotype, despite previous morpholino studies suggesting Urp1/Urp2 are required for straightening. This was confirmed using both germline mutants and crispants across multiple genetic backgrounds.
results.evaluation: Claims C42-C57 are well-supported by multiple lines of genetic evidence including germline mutations, crispant analysis, T7E1 validation of mutagenesis, and testing across multiple genetic backgrounds (AB, WIK, TU). The data directly contradict previous morpholino results, which the authors acknowledge and discuss extensively. The experimental design is rigorous with appropriate controls.

results.result: Loss of Urp1 and Urp2 causes adult-onset spinal curves in a semi-redundant manner. Single urp1ΔP mutants appear normal at 3 mpf but develop curves by 12 mpf, while urp2ΔP mutants show mild curves at 3 mpf that worsen by 12 mpf. Double mutants exhibit prominent dorsal-ventral curves with significant Cobb angles at 3 mpf, especially in the caudal spine region. The progressive worsening with age demonstrates that Urp1/Urp2 function throughout adulthood to maintain spine morphology, with Urp2 playing a larger role than Urp1.
results.evaluation: Claims C58-C67 are strongly supported by μCT imaging data at multiple time points (3 mpf and 12 mpf) with quantitative Cobb angle measurements. The semi-redundancy is clearly demonstrated by comparing single versus double mutant phenotypes. Sample sizes are adequate (n=7-92 depending on analysis). The age-related progression is well-documented.

results.result: Urp1 and Urp2 signal through the Uts2r3 receptor to control spine morphology. The authors generated uts2r3b1436 mutants harboring a 178-amino acid deletion. These mutants phenocopy urp1ΔP;urp2ΔP double mutants, showing normal embryonic straightening followed by adult-onset spinal curves with similar Cobb angles and predominantly caudal curve locations, though urp1ΔP;urp2ΔP curves are slightly more severe.
results.evaluation: Claims C68-C78 are well-supported by comparative phenotypic analysis between uts2r3 mutants and urp1/urp2 double mutants using μCT and quantitative measurements. The similarity in phenotypes provides strong genetic evidence for this receptor-ligand relationship. The authors appropriately note they cannot rule out minor roles for other UT receptors.

results.result: Spinal curves in urp1ΔP;urp2ΔP mutants onset during adolescent growth (9-11 dpf) when fish are rapidly growing, with curves evident in all mutants by 13 dpf. Curve location is dynamic during development, with pre-caudal curves common at 1 mpf but rare at 3 mpf. Calcein staining and μCT analysis revealed no major vertebral patterning defects, though mutants showed more variable vertebral length aspect ratios. Small vertebral shape changes are likely consequences rather than causes of curves. No sex bias in curve severity was observed.
results.evaluation: Claims C79-C89 are supported by longitudinal imaging studies, calcein staining, μCT analysis, and quantitative vertebral morphometry. The temporal analysis is well-documented with appropriate sample sizes. The statistical analysis of vertebral dimensions (Bartlett's test for equal variances) is appropriate. The interpretation that vertebral changes are secondary to curves rather than causative is reasonable given the lack of major structural defects.

results.result: Urotensin-deficient mutants are phenotypically distinct from cfap298tm304 (cilia motility) and pkd2l1icm02 mutants. cfap298tm304 mutants show more severe curves (260.4±32.7° total Cobb angle) than urp1ΔP;urp2ΔP (197.5±38.9°) or uts2r3b1436 (146.1±47.4°) mutants. cfap298tm304 mutants exhibit three-dimensional curves with both dorso-ventral and lateral deviations plus spinal twisting, while urotensin mutants show predominantly planar dorso-ventral curves in caudal vertebrae. Triple mutants (cfap298tm304;urp1ΔP;urp2ΔP) resemble cfap298tm304 single mutants, suggesting motile cilia contribute to both urotensin-dependent and urotensin-independent pathways. pkd2l1icm02 mutants show only mild kyphosis-like curves at 12 mpf, distinct from urotensin mutants.
results.evaluation: Claims C90-C111 are well-supported by systematic comparative analysis using μCT imaging, Cobb angle measurements, and lateral curvature quantitation across multiple mutant lines raised under identical conditions. The quantitative differences in curve severity, position, and three-dimensionality are clearly documented. The triple mutant analysis provides strong evidence for multiple pathways. Sample sizes are adequate for the comparisons made.

results.result: The Reissner fiber (RF) breaks down prior to curve formation in cfap298tm304 mutants but remains intact in uts2r3b1436 mutants. Using Sspo-GFP imaging, the authors showed that cfap298tm304 mutants lack RF at 28 hpf and show diffuse Sspo at 12 dpf before curves fully develop, demonstrating that cilia motility is required for both RF formation and maintenance. In contrast, uts2r3b1436 mutants maintain an intact RF at both 28 hpf and 12 dpf as curves begin to form, indicating that urotensin-associated curves occur through an RF-independent mechanism.
results.evaluation: Claims C11-C13 and C112-C136 are strongly supported by Sspo-GFP imaging data at multiple developmental stages (28 hpf and 12 dpf) in multiple genetic backgrounds. The temporal relationship between RF breakdown and curve formation in cfap298 mutants is well-documented. The intact RF in uts2r3 mutants despite curve formation provides clear evidence for an RF-independent mechanism. The imaging is qualitative but the differences are clear and consistent.

results.result: The authors propose a model where urotensin signals act downstream of RF function in controlling spine morphology. urp1 and urp2 expression is controlled by RF function during embryonic phases, as shown by reduced expression in cfap298tm304 and sspob1446 mutants. However, decreased urotensin signaling cannot fully account for spinal curves in cilia motility or RF mutants, as these mutants show more severe and three-dimensional curves. The differential expression of Urp1 (ventral CSF-cNs only) versus Urp2 (both dorsal and ventral CSF-cNs) may explain why urotensin mutants show planar dorso-ventral curves while cilia/RF mutants show three-dimensional curves.
results.evaluation: Claims C137-C147 are supported by qRT-PCR data showing reduced urp expression in cfap298 and sspo mutants, in situ hybridization showing differential expression patterns, and the phenotypic comparisons between mutant types. The model is logical and consistent with the data, though it remains somewhat speculative. The authors appropriately acknowledge complexity, including the finding that rpgrip1l mutation increases urp expression.

results.result: The authors address the discrepancy between their genetic results (no CTD in urp1/urp2 mutants) and previous morpholino studies (CTD in morphants). They argue against morpholino off-target effects based on peptide rescue experiments and the parsimony of Urp1/Urp2 functioning across life stages. They consider genetic compensation as a possible explanation, noting slight upregulation of urp2 in urp1ΔP mutants, though this cannot fully explain the lack of CTD in double mutants. A complementary study (Gaillard et al., 2022) independently confirmed no embryonic defects in urp1/urp2 mutants and found no upregulation of other urotensin genes, arguing against compensation. The authors conclude that Urp1/Urp2 are not essential for embryonic straightening but are required for maintenance during growth and adulthood.
results.evaluation: Claims C166-C177 are supported by the comprehensive genetic analysis (germline mutants, maternal-zygotic mutants, crispants) and corroboration from an independent study. The discussion of genetic compensation is thoughtful and appropriately cautious. The qRT-PCR data showing slight urp2 upregulation in urp1 mutants is documented. The conclusion that Urp1/Urp2 are dispensable for embryonic straightening is strongly supported, though the mechanism underlying the morpholino phenotype remains unexplained.

results.result: The authors compare zebrafish spinal anatomy to humans and argue that urotensin-deficient mutants model aspects of lordosis. Zebrafish and human spines are broadly similar with comparable loads, and both are predisposed to age-related curvature. Zebrafish have a natural kyphotic curve in pre-caudal vertebrae and minor lordotic curve in anterior caudal vertebrae, though less pronounced than humans. Urotensin mutants show planar dorso-ventral curves predominantly in caudal vertebrae without lateral deviation, similar to hyper-lordosis in humans. However, the authors acknowledge that human lumbar and zebrafish caudal vertebrae are structurally distinct, and zebrafish lack the significant natural lordotic curve associated with upright posture, so the model has limitations.
results.evaluation: Claims C154-C164 are supported by comparative anatomical observations and citations to relevant literature. The characterization of urotensin mutant curves as 'lordosis-like' is reasonable given the planar nature, caudal location, and lack of lateral deviation. The authors appropriately acknowledge the limitations of the model and the structural differences between zebrafish and humans. The comparison is thoughtful and appropriately cautious.

results.result: The authors discuss future research directions and potential relevance to human disease. They note that the target tissues for Urp1/Urp2 signaling remain unknown, though uts2r3 is expressed in multiple cell types including muscle. The timing of urotensin action is unclear - defects may occur earlier than phenotypes manifest. They cite evidence from Xenopus (Utr4 disruption causes body axis curvature) and human genetics (UTS2R mutations associated with AIS) suggesting conservation of urotensin function in spine morphology across species.
results.evaluation: Claims C178-C187 appropriately identify gaps in knowledge and future research needs. The citations to Xenopus and human studies provide evidence for potential conservation of function. These are reasonable speculations and suggestions for future work based on the current findings.

results.result: The authors provide background context on spine development, spinal deformities (scoliosis, kyphosis, lordosis), zebrafish as models for spinal deformity, the role of motile cilia and CSF flow, the Reissner fiber, and urotensin peptides. These claims establish the scientific context and rationale for the study.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C41 and C124-C129 are general knowledge claims supported by appropriate citations to the literature. These provide necessary background and context for understanding the significance of the work. The citations appear accurate and appropriate.

results.result: The abstract summarizes the main findings: Urp1 and Urp2 (10-amino acid cyclic peptides expressed by central canal neurons) are essential for maintaining zebrafish spine morphology. Combined loss causes adolescent-onset planar curves in the caudal spine without vertebral patterning defects. Similar curves occur in uts2r3 receptor mutants. Urotensin-associated curves are distinct from other zebrafish spinal curve mutants in position and direction.
results.evaluation: Claims C4-C10 accurately summarize the main findings that are supported by the detailed experimental data described in other result groups. These are appropriate summary statements for the abstract.

results.result: The authors note that temperature-shift experiments showed no role for motile cilia beyond 34 dpf in maintaining the spine, contrasting with the long-term role of urotensin peptides. However, they appropriately note this doesn't preclude a role for CSF flow or RF in adult spine maintenance, as it hasn't been determined if motile cilia are required for CSF flow or RF formation in adult fish.
results.evaluation: Claims C152-C153 accurately cite previous work and appropriately identify a gap in knowledge. The distinction between cilia function and CSF flow/RF maintenance in adults is an important caveat.
